security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU emulates sourcecfgK as a single flat register without zeroing/remapping fields when the D (delegation) bit transitions between 0 and 1 in M-domain. When D=0, bits 23:16 hold IPRIO and bits 2:0 hold SM; when D=1, bits 9:0 hold Child Index. A guest writes a value in one format, toggles D, then reads back the other format, observing stale bits from the previous format at aliased bit positions.
security_spec.summary: ACLIC sourcecfgK register format changes based on D bit — QEMU must zero/remap fields on D-bit transitions or else guest-stashed values in IPRIO/SM positions (D=0) become readable as Child-Index bits (D=1), leaking prior configuration state across delegation boundaries

findings.finding: QEMU's sourcecfg write uses a full register overwrite (aplic->sourcecfg[irq] = value) after masking the written value based on the new D bit. When D=1, value is masked to (D | CHILDIDX_MASK), zeroing bits 31:11 and 9:3. When D=0, value is masked to (D | SM_MASK), zeroing bits 31:11 and 9:3. Since the entire 32-bit register is replaced each write, no stale bits from a prior format survive across a D-bit toggle. The read path returns the raw stored value, which is safe because only valid-field bits are ever stored.

spec_citations.excerpt: When accessing the source configuration via indirect CSR, only the lower 16b are accessible, as the rest of the register is reserved... ACLIC simplifies Child Index to always 0 when D=1, and D is always 0 in Supervisor mode.

findings.finding: When num_children==0, writes with D=1 are forced to 0 (WARL constraint), preventing invalid delegation to a non-existent child domain. This prevents an attacker from setting D=1 on a domain with no children and then observing stale CHILDIDX bits.

Post-write side-effects are correct: when D=1 or SM=INACTIVE (sourcecfg==0), pending and enabled bits are atomically cleared. When transitioning to active, the rectified input is re-evaluated and pending is set if appropriate. No side-effect gaps.
sourcecfg array is g_new0-allocated, resetting all entries to 0 (D=0, SM=INACTIVE) as mandated by the spec for inactive sources.
sourcecfg array is included in the VMState migration descriptors, ensuring correct live migration of per-source configuration state.

QEMU currently has no ACLIC indirect-CSR interface (Smidctrl/Ssidctrl via xiselect-based ireg2/ireg3 for sourcecfg). If such support is added (in target/riscv/csr.c), the indirect CSR path must implement its own D-bit-aware masking and full-register-replacement semantics, separate from this memory-mapped handler. Currently this is a non-issue since ACLIC CSR emulation does not exist in QEMU.

spec_citations.excerpt: Source Configuration (sourcecfg): When XLEN=32, xireg2 and xireg3 combined control source configuration of four interrupts. Indirect access to aclicsourcecfg[k] mirrors sourcecfg[k*2][15:0].
